content.overview: Specialists should classify environmental faults from evidence before recommending qualified service. Trend data should connect commands, equipment state, sensor response and crop-zone outcome.

vocabulary.definition: A condition where a controller command occurs but the expected equipment or environmental response does not follow.
A bounded category such as sensor, distribution, capacity, sequencing or equipment-response problem.
A structured escalation package sent to the role authorized to service the suspected system.

sections.title: Follow the sequence from command to crop
sections.body: Review controller request, equipment status, representative sensor response and crop-zone outcome. A command alone does not prove the system delivered the intended environment.

sections.title: Classify before naming root cause
sections.body: Evidence may support a sensor fault, airflow-distribution problem, latent-capacity limitation or equipment non-response without proving the exact mechanical failure.

sections.title: Handoff the evidence, not a repair instruction
sections.body: Record timestamps, affected zones, alarms, equipment states, verified measurements and safe boundaries for the qualified maintenance or controls role.

workedExamples: A dehumidification command is logged, equipment status never changes, and canopy RH continues rising; the evidence supports an equipment-response fault class even before the mechanical cause is known.
commonMistakes: Calling a controller command proof of delivery.
Opening electrical or HVAC equipment to verify a suspected fault.
Deleting conflicting sensor data from the handoff.
content.practicalApplication: Build a command-response timeline and a maintenance handoff from a supplied environmental trend.
content.summary: Strong environmental troubleshooting narrows the fault class and transfers evidence safely to the qualified role.
